items.title: `&`, `\|`, `^` over two DIFFERENT integer types (`i32 & usize`), and any bitwise operator over a float (`f64 & f64`, `f64 & i32`), check clean — B579/B602 refuse only `-`, `*`, `/`, `%`; JS coerces silently, the native build refuses
items.body: `vilan check` clean; `vilan run` prints JS's coercions (an f64 truncated to int32); `--backend rust` refuses "does not emit an operator over two numeric types (`i32` and `usize`)" (and rustc has no `BitAnd` for `f64`). The B579 arm (finalize_build's binary-operator check) is the model: refuse a mixed integer pair under `&`/`\|`/`^` (shifts are legal across integer types in Rust, so leave `<<`/`>>`/`>>>` mixed), and a float operand under any bitwise operator with a sentence of its own. Likely BREAKING (count the estate). Sizing S; solver.

items.title: B598's static twin: `List::describe([1, 2])` in a file importing only `pkg::describe::Describe` is refused "'describe' is not an inherent member of 'List': 'Wire' and 'Describe' provide it; call 'Wire::describe(..)' or 'Describe::describe(..)'" — the steer names std's `Wire`, which the file does not reach
items.body: B598 narrows a METHOD call's trait candidates to the traits the calling file reaches (B515's rule); the static path (`Type::member`, the static-accessor arm of resolve_world that ranks `method_member_candidates`) does not, so its refusal names an unreachable trait. Apply `candidates_reached_at` there too (it is a refusal either way — a trait method is not an inherent static — but the steer should name only `Describe::describe(..)`). Sizing S; solver.

items.title: a blanket's static named on a head its bound does not admit (`i32::tag(1)` over `impl type T: Leaf with Tag`) says only "cannot find 'tag' in i32" — it could say `i32` is not `Leaf`, which the blanket providing `tag` requires
items.body: After B595 the satisfied head resolves (`str::tag(1)`); the unsatisfied one falls to the generic not-found sentence because the candidate scan drops the blanket by its bound. Name the blanket and the missing bound ("`tag` is provided by `impl type T: Leaf with Tag`, and `i32` does not implement `Leaf`"). Sizing XS; solver.

items.title: the native emitter's in-body anchor note ("The construct is in `is_some`'s body (`option.vl`), which this call instantiates", vilan-rust lib.rs) has no reachable std probe after B600: the probe it used (`Option::None.is_some()`) is refused at `vilan check` now, as F108's `push_many([])` was before it
items.body: B600 refuses an open instance at the check, so the F108 pin now asserts the check's refusal at the user's call; the in-body note is unpinned. Either find another construct the native backend refuses inside a std body that the checker admits (each such construct is itself a check/build disagreement worth filing), or pin the note at the emitter level with a synthetic program. Sizing XS; native.
